READ-ONLY audit of /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma + systemd worker). Do NOT modify any file, do not run builds, do not write to DB.

Your scope: the customer webmail + business email hosting:
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/email/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/** (MailClient, MailSettings, Composer, ReadingPane, MessageList, FolderRail, ContactPanel, ShortcutHelp, util)
- /opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx, EmailDnsSetup.tsx, CloudflareConnect.tsx, CloudflareIntegration.tsx
- backing: /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mail.ts, lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts, lib/actions-email-hosting.ts, lib/mail/**, lib/mailcow.ts, lib/cloudflare*.ts

I am hunting DEAD or LYING UI. Definition:
- A control (button/toggle/form/select) that calls nothing, or calls an action nobody consumes.
- A preference persisted to the DB where NO code anywhere reads that column to change behaviour. THE JACKPOT: settings the user configures in MailSettings.tsx that are written to the Mailbox table but never pushed to Mailcow / never affect actual mail delivery or composition. Specifically investigate: forwardingAddress, forwardKeepCopy, replyTo, organization, autoReplyEnabled/autoReplySubject/autoReplyBody, autoReplyStart, autoReplyEnd, signatureEnabled, signatureOnReply, signaturePlacement, displayName. For EACH, trace: is it read at send time (SMTP), at receive time, or pushed to Mailcow? Or only read back to re-render its own settings form?
- Status text/badges that cannot reflect reality.
- Success toasts shown unconditionally even when the call failed.
- Forms submitting to an action that returns success but silently no-ops.
- Links/buttons navigating to routes that 404.

VERIFY every finding by reading the code. For each give ABSOLUTE file:line and a CONCRETE failure scenario ("customer sets vacation auto-reply, UI says saved, but senders never get a reply because X"). Drop anything you cannot make concrete. Depth beats breadth.

Return findings directly as your final message. Do NOT write any file. Also state which parts you checked and found SOLID.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Dead / Lying UI audit — customer webmail + business email hosting

## THE JACKPOT: the "Identity" panel is entirely decorative

`MailSettings.tsx` → `IdentitySection` writes three columns to `Mailbox`. **None of the three is ever read by anything except the form that wrote it.** There is no disclaimer on this section (unlike Auto-reply and Forwarding, which do carry honest warnings — see below).

The send path is the proof. `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mail.ts:430-441` compiles every outgoing message:

```ts
const built = await composer.sendMail({
  from: cred.address,     // <- bare address, nothing else
  to: to.list, cc: ..., bcc: ..., subject, text, html, attachments, inReplyTo, references,
});
```

`cred` is built at `/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/imap.ts:119` as `{ address, password }` only. `sendMessage` never loads the `Mailbox` row's identity columns, and there is no `replyTo`, no `headers`, and no `Organization` anywhere in the file.

**1. `displayName` — dead.** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx:234` claims *"Shown as the sender name on messages you send."*
Written at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:166`. Read back only at `:108` to refill the input. Not read at send time; not pushed to Mailcow — `mcCreateMailbox` is called once at provisioning with `name: mailbox.address` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:105`), and `/opt/nxeon/lib/mailcow.ts` has **no** "edit mailbox name" helper at all.
*Failure:* customer types "Jane Doe — Acme Support", sees "Saved.", sends a mail. Recipient's inbox shows `jane@acme.com`, not `Jane Doe`. Reopening settings shows "Jane Doe" persisted, so the customer concludes it works and never reports it.

**2. `replyTo` — dead.** `MailSettings.tsx:260` claims *"Replies are directed here instead of your sending address."*
Written at `actions-mailbox-settings.ts:172` (with full email validation, which makes it look load-bearing). Read back only at `:109`. No `replyTo` key is ever passed to nodemailer.
*Failure:* a business sets Reply-To to `support@acme.com` so customer replies land in the shared helpdesk. Every reply instead goes to the individual's personal mailbox. Silent, and the misrouting is invisible until the helpdesk notices it is empty.

**3. `organization` — dead.** Validated and stored at `actions-mailbox-settings.ts:178`, read back at `:110`. Never emitted as an `Organization:` header.
Its only other consumer is client-side cosmetic: `MailSettings.tsx:566` seeds the *signature template* picker text. So it affects the signature editor's suggested boilerplate, nothing on the wire.

## Business email hosting

**4. Hardcoded mailbox status badge — cannot ever reflect reality.**
`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:345`:

```tsx
<Badge tone="amber">Provisioning</Badge>
```

It is a literal. The `MailboxRow` type at `EmailHosting.tsx:24` is `{ id, address, createdAt }` — no `status` field — and `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/email/page.tsx:51-55` deliberately drops `m.status` when mapping.

Meanwhile the real column moves: `ACTIVE` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:112`, `FAILED` at `:117`, `SUSPENDED` at `:624`.
*Failure:* Mailcow is down when the customer adds `hello@acme.com`. `provisionMailboxOnMailcow` catches, sets `FAILED` (`:117`), and returns without throwing (`addMailbox` still returns `{ok:true}`). The customer sees the mailbox listed with an amber "Provisioning" badge. It will still say "Provisioning" next week, next month, forever. The mailbox does not exist on the mail server, mail to it bounces, and nothing in the UI ever says so. A working `ACTIVE` mailbox and a suspended-for-non-payment mailbox render identically.

**5. The two actions that would fix #4 have zero consumers.**
`retryMailboxProvision` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:545`) — 0 references anywhere in `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `worker/`, `scripts/`.
`setMailboxSuspended` (`:606`) — 0 references.
The module docstring at `:65` and `:69` advertises retry as part of *"customer mailbox management"*, and `:489` calls a failed row *"(retryable)"*. There is no retry control in `MailboxItem` — only Show password / Reset password / Remove. A customer whose provisioning failed has no path forward except deleting and re-adding the mailbox.

**6. `EmailSubscription.verified` gates nothing — three false claims hang off it.**
`verifyEmailDomain` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:418-480`) resolves the TXT token, then does exactly one thing: `data: { verified: true, verifiedAt: new Date() }` (`:466-469`). It does not touch Mailcow, does not provision or re-provision anything.

A repo-wide grep for `.verified` shows it is consumed **only** for rendering: `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx:46`, `EmailHosting.tsx:236`, `EmailDnsSetup.tsx:91`. It gates no code path — not `addMailbox`, not provisioning, not IMAP/SMTP, not billing.

Conversely, `addMailbox` (`:491-539`) has **no** verification check and calls `provisionMailboxOnMailcow` immediately at `:530`, which itself creates the domain on Mailcow at `:95-99`. So mailboxes go live at *creation* time, and mail flows the moment the customer's MX points at the host — the `_nxeon-verify` TXT record is irrelevant to delivery.

Three statements are therefore untrue:
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:96-97` — *"mail starts flowing once verification succeeds"*
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailDnsSetup.tsx:137-139` — *"Mail won't flow until you add these records at your DNS provider and verification succeeds. Mailboxes you create now are saved and go live once verified."*
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailDnsSetup.tsx:106` — *"DNS verified — mail is now enabled for this domain."*

*Failure (both directions):* (a) A customer adds MX + SPF but skips the `_nxeon-verify` TXT record. Their mail already works perfectly, yet the panel shows a red-amber "Verification required" block insisting mail won't flow — so they open a support ticket about mail that isn't broken. (b) A customer adds only the TXT record, clicks Verify DNS, gets the green "Verified — mail is enabled" badge, and stops. Without MX, no mail is delivered at all. The badge actively told them setup was finished.

## Webmail client

**7. Attachment downloads break on any non-default mailbox.** *(genuine correctness bug, not just cosmetic)*
`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/ReadingPane.tsx:174` builds the link:

```
/api/mail/attachment?folder=...&uid=...&part=...
```

No `&mailbox=` parameter. `ReadingPane` is never given the active address — `MailClient.tsx:628-642` passes `message`, `folders`, `currentFolder` and callbacks, but not `activeAddress` (every *other* call site threads it through). The route reads `sp.get("mailbox")` (`/opt/nxeon/app/api/mail/attachment/route.ts:19`) and passes `undefined` to `resolveMailbox`, which falls back to `boxes[0]` — the oldest mailbox on the account (`/opt/nxeon/lib/mail/imap.ts:101`).
*Failure:* a user with `sales@` (created first) and `jane@` switches to `jane@`, opens an invoice, clicks the PDF. The server opens `sales@`'s INBOX and fetches that UID. Best case a 404; worst case the UID happens to exist and **the customer downloads a different message's attachment from a different mailbox**. Same class of bug applies to any shared-team account with multiple boxes.

**8. "Starred" only searches the newest 50 inbox messages.**
`MailClient.tsx:191` maps the Starred pseudo-folder to `inboxPath`, then `:207-209` filters the returned page client-side. Page size is 50 (`actions-mail.ts:46`) and `:609` pins `page={selected === STARRED ? 1 : page}`, so pagination cannot reach further.
*Failure:* a user stars an important message, then archives it — or simply receives 50 newer emails. Clicking "Starred" shows "No messages / This folder is empty." The star is still set on the server; the view just cannot see it. There is no IMAP `\Flagged` search across folders anywhere in `actions-mail.ts`.

**9. "Snoozed" is a permanently empty folder with no feature behind it.**
`MailClient.tsx:167` pushes it into the rail as a normal, enabled nav item; `:190` returns `null` for its path, so `loadList` short-circuits to an empty list (`:200-203`). `MessageList` then renders the generic empty state — *"This folder is empty. New mail will show up here."* (`MessageList.tsx:304`) — which is untrue: nothing can ever arrive there. There is no snooze column in the schema and no snooze action.
This is inconsistent with how the same codebase honestly handles the rest of the feature: the Snooze toolbar button is `disabled` with `title="Snooze — coming soon"` (`ReadingPane.tsx:92`), and the Filters button likewise (`FolderRail.tsx:110-111`). The rail entry should get the same treatment.

**10. Storage panel reports "0 MB used" instead of admitting the probe failed.**
`MailSettings.tsx:1065` computes `haveUsage = usedBytes !== undefined`, and `:1088` uses it to show *"live usage is unavailable right now; showing your plan quota."* That branch is unreachable. `getMailboxes` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mail.ts:70-93`) initialises `usedBytes = 0` and, on any IMAP QUOTA/STATUS failure, swallows the error (`:88-90`) and pushes the `0` anyway.
*Failure:* a mailbox holding 4 GB whose quota probe throws renders "0 MB of 5 GB — 0% used" with an empty progress bar. The customer believes they have a fresh mailbox; the near-full warning at `:1089` can never fire for exactly the users who most need it.

**11. Pagination counter ignores the active category tab.**
`MessageList.tsx:58` filters rows by tab (`filtered`), but `:61-62` compute `start`/`end`/`totalPages` from the unfiltered folder `total`.
*Failure:* user clicks "Promotions"; 3 of the 50 fetched messages match. The footer still reads "1–50 of 1,240" above 3 visible rows, and the next-page arrow pages the *underlying folder*, so the tab contents jump unpredictably.

**12. Minor — shortcut help overstates six shortcuts.**
`ShortcutHelp.tsx:10-15` lists `r`, `a`, `f`, `e`, `#`, `s` unconditionally, but `MailClient.tsx:520-525` gates every one on `if (message)` — i.e. a message must be *open in the reading pane*. Moving the cursor with `j`/`k` in the list and pressing `s` to star, or `e` to archive, does nothing and gives no feedback.

## Checked and found SOLID

- **Signature pipeline — fully wired end to end.** This is the counter-example that proves the Identity fields are a genuine defect rather than a house style. `signatureHtml`/`signatureEnabled`/`signatureOnReply`/`signaturePlacement` are loaded per-mailbox at `MailClient.tsx:125-137`, correctly gated in `sigFields` (`:144-155`, including the reply-specific opt-out), spread into the draft, and consumed at `Composer.tsx:167-186` — where `signaturePlacement` genuinely reorders `userDiv`/`sigHtml`/`quoteHtml`. Re-sanitised server-side (`actions-mailbox-settings.ts:182`) and client-side, with a plain-text fallback derived into the legacy column for the `text/plain` part.
- **Send result handling is honest.** `MailClient.tsx:391-398` throws on `{ok:false}` *before* `setToast("Message sent.")`, and `Composer.submit` only calls `onClose()` after `onSend` resolves (`Composer.tsx:194-208`). No unconditional success toast anywhere in the mail client.
- **Aliases** — real Mailcow round-trips with ownership checks on the domain (`actions-mailbox-settings.ts:295-369`), optimistic removal correctly rolled back via `load()` on failure (`MailSettings.tsx:1186-1200`).
- **Password reset** — genuinely applies on Mailcow and surfaces real errors; no fake success path.
- **Attachment API route** — auth and ownership enforced through `resolveMailbox`, `no-store`, `nosniff`, and it even tolerates the `uid:partId` id form (`route.ts:17-19`). The only defect is the missing `mailbox` param on the caller's side (#7).
- **Keyboard shortcuts** — every key in the help modal is implemented (`MailClient.tsx:510-537`), with correct typing-field suppression and a stable-ref handler that avoids stale state.
- **`disconnectCloudflare`** — the claim at `CloudflareIntegration.tsx:86` (*"revokes it at Cloudflare"*) is true: `actions-cloudflare.ts:106-108` calls `cfRevoke` for OAuth connections before clearing the local record.
- **`CloudflarePanel` / `autoCreateEmailDns`** — wired, reports the actual created record names back from the server (`EmailDnsSetup.tsx:226-231`), and correctly tells the user to still run Verify DNS.
- **Rate limiting and ownership checks** across `actions-mail.ts` and `actions-mailbox-settings.ts` are consistent and real — every action resolves through `resolveMailbox`, which re-checks ownership server-side.

**Suggested priority:** #6 and #4 first (they cause support tickets and misdirect customers during onboarding), then #1-3 (silent, long-lived, and trivially fixable — three lines in the nodemailer call at `actions-mail.ts:430`), then #7 (data-correctness).
